newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat in Hebron tells settlers "we want peace".
newsitem.headline: Arafat in Hebron tells settlers "we want peace".

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Hebron on Sunday and told Jewish settlers who remain in the largely PLO-ruled city he wanted peace.

Arafat laid claim to Hebron, the prize of months of bitter negotiations with Israel's right-wing leader Benjamin Netanyahu, in a speech to 25,000 supporters on a hill above the city, revered by Jews and Moslems as Abraham's birthplace.
"I tell settlers we do not want confrontation," the former guerrilla chief said, having flown by helicopter to the hilltop headquarters of Israel's 30-year-long occupation that ended on Friday.
Settler leaders dismissed Arafat's assurance.

Arafat said Hebron was a springboard for further Israeli withdrawals in the West Bank. He said Israel would release Palestinian women prisoners in a few days followed by the eventual release of Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, the spiritual leader of the Islamic fundamentalist Hamas movement.
"Hebron is a springboard for what comes after...so that we can establish our independent Palestinian state, you have a big responsibility," Arafat said in Arabic.
"A promise is a promise, we will continue to Jerusalem," he added to applause.
Arafat has made the same promise about making Arab East Jerusalem his capital in every Palestinian town he has "liberated" since arriving in Gaza in July 1994 to lead the self-rule Authority.

The agreement on Hebron, reached after much diplomatic arm-twisting by the United States, has revived hopes that Arafat and Prime Minister Netanyahu can see the wider self-rule accord through to a final resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, including issues like settlements and Jerusalem, in 1999.
Palestinians had decorated the 80 percent of Hebron under their control with Palestinian flags and posters for the man they call "Abu Ammar".
Arafat's stubbled jowls smiled down from a mural erected on a hill overlooking the enclaves where some 400 armed Jewish settlers live and study in the heart of the town of 100,000 Palestinians.
The settlers call Arafat a murderer and see the agreement with Netanyahu as a betrayal of their biblical right to all of the West Bank.
Both Arab and Jew fear violence from each other in Hebron where some 2,000 Israeli soldiers will stay to protect the settlers.
"If these Jewish settlers in Hebron who have been provocative to Palestinans here do not make problems there will be no problems in Hebron," said West Bank Palestinian security chief Jibril Rajoub.
He is in charge of the 400 uniformed police and an undisclosed number of plainclothes police who deployed in Hebron after the last Israeli soldiers slipped away at dawn on Friday.

But Palestinian security sources said more than the 400 police stipulated under the deal were in the city along with several hundred plainclothes police, with Israel's tacit approval. The sources said Rajoub would move his headquarters to Hebron from Jericho.

Rajoub, whose forces have been accused of human rights violations by civil rights groups, told Reuters: "We will punish any Palestinian who violates the law and any policeman who maltreats Palestinians will also be punished."
Settler spokesman David Wilder said he was not reassured by Arafat's speech, noting that Arafat had claimed East Jerusalem.
"The only way he can do that is through violence," Wilder said.
Arafat urged East Jerusalem's 150,000 residents to resist Israel's Judaization of the city.
"I tell our people in Jerusalem they have to protect the Arab character of Jerusalem," he added, referring to Israel's vast building programme for Jews in the divided city.
Arafat said Israel would free Palestinian women prisoners "within a few days" in line with the peace agreement.

The release of prisoners, especially the blind, wheelchair-bound Yassin, would shore up Arafat's support among Palestinians on the street, including in Hebron, a stronghold of Moslem militant activism.
"I tell the shabiba (activists) that your brother Sheikh Ahmed Yassin will be released soon," Arafat said.
